title: Multiorbital periodic Anderson model for CeRh2As2
authors: Nico A. Hackner, Changhee Lee, P. M. R. Brydon
abstract: CeRh2As2 is a heavy-fermion superconductor that exhibits distinct low- and high-field superconducting phases, widely interpreted as reflecting a field-induced change in the parity of the order parameter. However, the superconductivity develops in close proximity to magnetic order whose microscopic origin and nature remain unclear. Moreover, the low-lying crystal-electric-field-split doublets of the Ce 4f electrons appear to realize an unusual "quasi-quartet" structure. This has motivated proposals that quadrupolar degrees of freedom play an important role in the low-temperature physics. Here we develop a microscopic heavy-fermion description of CeRh2As2 that incorporates both the quasi-quartet structure and the nonsymmorphic symmetry. Within a multiorbital periodic Anderson model, we include the lowest-lying $Γ_7$ and $Γ_6$ doublets of the Ce 4f electrons, and allow for nonlocal hybridization with the conduction d electrons. Single occupancy of the 4f states is enforced within the rotationally invariant slave-boson formalism. Adopting a mean-field treatment, we first show that the effective low-energy Hamiltonian is accurately captured by a single-orbital tight-binding model, justifying the minimal descriptions widely employed in the literature. Allowing for a magnetic ground state, we find that our model displays metallic $\mathbf{Q}=(π,π)$ antiferromagnetic order over a wide parameter regime. Ferromagnetic solutions also occur, but in a smaller region of parameter space and with greater sensitivity to carrier concentration and the form of the f-d hybridization. Quadrupolar moments appear only within magnetically ordered phases and are generally small, becoming substantial only when the $Γ_7$ and $Γ_6$ doublets are nearly degenerate. Our results provide a microscopic basis for understanding the itinerant heavy-fermion physics and ordered phases of CeRh2As2.
summary: This work develops a multiorbital periodic Anderson model for CeRh2As2 to address the complex interplay between superconductivity, magnetism, and crystal field effects. Using a slave-boson mean-field approach, the authors predict the nature of the magnetic ground state and establish the conditions under which quadrupolar degrees of freedom become important. The results provide a detailed microscopic framework for understanding itinerant heavy-fermion physics in this material.
main_problem: The paper aims to microscopically understand the superconductivity and magnetic/quadrupolar ordering in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2, focusing on the role of the Ce 4f electrons.
main_result: The model predicts stable metallic antiferromagnetic order with Q=(pi, pi) and shows that quadrupolar moments become substantial only when the relevant f-electron doublets are nearly degenerate.
method: The authors developed and applied a multiorbital periodic Anderson model within the rotationally invariant slave-boson formalism, followed by a mean-field treatment.
model_or_system: The system is CeRh2As2, modeled by a PAM incorporating the lowest-lying $\Gamma_7$ and $\Gamma_6$ doublets of the Ce 4f electrons and nonlocal hybridization with conduction d electrons.
key_observables: Magnetic order parameters (AFM Q=(pi, pi)), quadrupolar moments, and the effective low-energy Hamiltonian.
important_parameters: Hybridization strength, electron filling, and the degeneracy between the $\Gamma_7$ and $\Gamma_6$ doublets.
main_assumptions: The use of the slave-boson formalism enforces single occupancy of 4f states, and the analysis relies on mean-field approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the paramagnetic saddle point and the dipole moments associated with various candidate magnetic states (e.g., FMz, A-AFMz).
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the multiorbital PAM, applies the slave-boson formalism, minimizes the free energy to find stable ordered states, and analyzes the symmetry constraints on these magnetic and quadrupolar orders.
why_interesting: While focused on heavy fermions, the rigorous use of symmetry analysis (e.g., in Chunk 4) and the development of a complex interacting Hamiltonian framework are highly relevant to understanding correlated quantum materials dynamics.
